summary: Friedrich Carl von Savigny worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the universities of Marburg, Jena, and Leipzig, and held posts at the University of Marburg (~1800–1808) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1842).
Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he studied at Heidelberg University (~1850–1852), Trinity College, Cambridge (1852), and the University of Paris, and studied under Theodor Goldstücker.

A linguist, Friedrich Christian Diez studied at the universities of Giessen and Göttingen, as well as under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1818–1820). He held a post at the University of Bonn from ~1822 to 1876.

Creuzer worked in religious studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. After studying at the universities of Tübingen and Jena, he held posts at the University of Marburg (~1800–1804), Leiden University (1809), and Heidelberg University (~1804–1845).

Delitzsch worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Jena under Brockhaus, Weber, Fleischer, Dillmann, Schrader, Curtius, and Windisch. He held professorships at Leipzig (1877), Breslau (1893), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1899).
Friedrich Ernst August Krause worked in Sinology. He studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1904–1907) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1925–1942).

Linguist Friedrich Ernst Kieckers studied at Bonn, Munich, Marburg, Berlin, and Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen. He held posts at Freiburg (1911) and Munich (1912, 1917), and was professor of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Tartu (1921–1938).

Welcker worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Giessen (~1801–1803), he held posts at Giessen (~1808–1816), the University of Göttingen (~1816–1819), and the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

Haag worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Göttingen. He held posts at several schools, as Dozent at Zurich (1873–1884), and as professor at Bern (1887–1914).

Heiler worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich under Hommel, Dyroff, Kieckers, Kuhn, and Scherman. He held posts at Munich (1918, 1962), Greifswald (1934), Marburg (1920–1962), and the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1928–1962).

Sinologist and historian Friedrich Hirth studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Greifswald, and Rostock. He served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897), the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1897–1902), and Columbia University as Dean Lung Professor (1902–1917).

Friedrich Karl Ginzel worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as an assistant at the Sternwarte von Oppolzer (1877–1886) and at the Astronomisches Rechen-Institut beginning in 1886.

Slotty worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Greifswald, Breslau, and Jena under Carl Cappeller and Berthold Delbrück. He held posts at Jena (1912, 1919, 1953–1954), Charles University (1925), and the German University in Prague (1928–1939).

Linguist Friedrich Kluge studied at Leipzig, Strasbourg, and Freiburg under August Leskien, Georg Curtius, and Heinrich Hübschmann. He held posts at Strasbourg (1880), the University of Jena (1884, 1886), and the University of Freiburg (1893).

Knauer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tartu under Leo Meyer and Leopold von Schroeder, Jena under Delbrück and Cappeller, and Tübingen under von Roth. He held posts at Tartu (1884) and Kyiv (1886–1914).
Linguist Friedrich Kurschat studied at the University of Königsberg from ~1836 to 1840. He subsequently held a post at the University of Königsberg from ~1841 to 1883.
Friedrich Leberecht Wilhelm Schwartz worked in linguistics, religious studies, and other fields. He completed his studies at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Leipzig.

Leo worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn, studying under Hermann Usener. He held posts at Bonn (1877–1881), Kiel (1881–1883), Rostock (1883–1888), Strasbourg (1888–1889), and Göttingen (1889–1914).
Friedrich Lorentz was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1890–1894), where he earned a Ph.D. and was taught by Karl Brugmann and August Leskien.

Friedrich Majer worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied law at the University of Jena (1791) and was a pupil of Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1790–1800). He served as Privatdozent at Jena (~1801–1804).
